name: Roman-style stone town gatehouse, 3/4 top-down: crenellated walkable top platform seen from above (windlass drum, portcullis pit with grate, stone balls, barrel), corbelled front face with a deep round arch tunnel (vault ribs, raised portcullis, darker toward the inside, paved road through), two wall torches
label: beodeul_town_wall/gatehouse_open

surfaces.part: walkable top platform (floor with windlass drum, portcullis pit, stone balls, barrel)
windlass drum, barrel and stone balls on platform
corbelled front face with arch tunnel and portcullis

answer.evidence: The upper part of the gatehouse (rows 11-46) is a large floor seen from above, with a crenellated back parapet in rows 0-10 and platform items such as the windlass, pit grate, stone balls and barrel. The platform ends in a dark front-edge line at row 47. Corbel and machicolation slots in rows 48-55 act as eave shadow, and the front face continues below with brick courses, a round arch, a raised portcullis and a paved tunnel through row 127. The top surface is about 36 rows and the front face about 80 rows. No receding side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 15 visible tones per 16x16 tile against 12 and 10 for the references. Its near-flat coverage is 3% (references 0%), so there are no large flat fills. Only 4% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outlines lean toward the stone (a dark blue-grey) and are not a uniform black sticker line. The stone is shaded block by block, with a lighter coping on the crenellations, a darker corbel course, and a deep vault that darkens toward the inside. The portcullis grate and the paved road add grain. The platform props (windlass, barrel, balls, pit) read as separate forms through value alone. The stone ramp has about 5 steps, slightly under the references' 6, and the small banners and torches are simple. Overall it would sit acceptably next to the references at the same scale.

answer.evidence: The upper ~47 rows (0-47) show a platform seen from above. It has a back parapet with merlons at rows 0-10, a floor with a windlass, grate, barrel and stones at rows 11-37, and front merlons at rows 38-46. A dark front-edge line at row 47 closes it. Below it, rows 48-127 form a tall vertical south face with a corbel band, stone courses, a deep round arch tunnel and torches. The platform contents (drum, barrel, balls) are decor. The structure has both a clear top surface and a front face of far more than 3 rows.

styleAnswer.evidence: Measured facts favour the candidate: 15 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, 3% near-flat coverage against 0%, and only 4% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outlines are tinted. By eye, the stone blocks carry about 4-5 grey steps, each block is shaded and speckled, and the arch interior darkens inward with a visible grate. Outlines are cool dark grey-blue, a tinted tone of the stone rather than a black sticker line. The top platform is the weakest part: the crenellations, windlass and barrel are small and read as simple, and the platform floor looks a bit flat and the tile detail thinner than the reference roofs with their per-tile highlights. The banners and torches are small flat accents. Overall it is close to the reference craft, though slightly less textured than the roof scallops and timber detail of the references. It is borderline, but the measured facts and structure hold up, so it passes.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 15 visible tones per 16x16 tile, against 12 and 10 for the references.
